paragraphs: On Monday, August seventeenth, a postcard comes for Tom and Lily. It is from Uncle Dan, Dad's brother. He is on holiday on an island far from home. The front shows a sunny coast with palm trees and boats with white sails. The words on the front say, "Greetings from the island!" Tom and Lily hold the card and look at the photo. "What does the sea look like?" asks Lily. "Read the card," says Tom.

Uncle Dan wrote the card on Wednesday, August twelfth. On the back, the message is on the left. On the right, there are a stamp and the words "Tom and Lily." Tom turns the card over and reads the message out loud. "Dear Tom and Lily, greetings from the island!" "The weather is hot and sunny, and the water is warm." "On Monday I sailed on a boat, and the waves were big." "From the boat, the sea looks like blue glass."

"Today I am doing some sightseeing in the little town." "The market sounds like a party, and it is full of tourists." "I write this card at a small café by the beach." "My hotel is on the coast, near the little town." "I wear my sunglasses all day." "My suitcase is full of presents for you." "I have never eaten so much fruit, and it is very tasty." "It tastes like sugar!" "I will be home on Sunday, August twenty-third." "Say hello to Pip." "Love, Uncle Dan."

"It sounds like a great holiday," says Tom. Pip comes and sniffs the stamp. Lily looks at the photo again. "I want to see that sea," she says. "Can we write to him?" asks Lily. "No, he comes home on Sunday," says Tom. "Then we can ask him about the fruit." "And we can ask about the big waves," says Lily. Tom puts the card on the fridge.
text.summary: A postcard from Uncle Dan comes to Tom and Lily. He writes about the weather, the sea, the fruit, and his holiday on an island.
